chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Hafs Al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guest, when he comes and lodges with a people, brings his sustenance with him from the sky. So when he eats, Allah forgives them due to his lodging among them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for hosting a guest in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this tradition linking the physical act of hosting to spiritual sustenance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the reciprocal rights between host and guest. The narrative suggests that the guest's presence is a divine blessing that triggers forgiveness for the host, reinforcing the social ethic of generosity as a means of spiritual purification.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn Al farsy, from Suleyman Bin Hafs Al Basry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The guest, when he comes over and lodges with a people, comes with his sustenance along with him, from the sky. So when he eats, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives for them (their sins) due to him having lodged with them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn al-Farsiy from Sulayman ibn Hafs ibn al-Basriy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith. ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “
When a guest comes and disembarks with a people, he comes with his sustenance from the sky. When he eats Allah forgives them because of his staying with them/”
